caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 239 of 1995.
lawyer:
Md. Abdus Samad Miah with Sontash Kumar Sarker, Advocate ----- For the Appellant.
Humayun Kabir Khadem, Advocate ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
AKM Shahidul Hoque ------ Appellant
Vs
Deputy Commissioner and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: The plaintiff presented the above appeal against the decree dated 30-4-95 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Court No. 1 at Rangpur in Money Suit No. 6 of 1993, which decreed the suit in part. 

 2. The plaintiff instituted the suit for a money decree of Taka 8,34,160 for the price of work done together with compensation. 

 9. On the pleadings, various issues as to maintainability of the suit; the valuation and payment of court-fees, entitlement of the plaintiff for any money for works done beyond the tender or to any decree of money were settled. 

 11. The learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiff was entitled to Taka 2,33,000 out of the estimated cost of Taka 11,33,000. After deducting the income tax at the rate of 1.5% from said amount and adding the earnest money deposited by the plaintiff, he held that the plaintiff was entitled to Taka 2,43,505 only. With regard to the claim of the plaintiff for Taka 3,88,887.81 for price of extra works, he found that as the works was done without any approval, the Hospital authority was not bound to pay for such works. Accordingly, by the impugned decree the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit in part for Taka 2,43,505 only with interest at Bank rate till realisation. 

 12. Mr Md Abdus Samad, the learned Advocate for the appellant, submits that it is not disputed that the plaintiff did extra work beyond the tender for which the plaintiff was entitled to Taka 3,88,887.81. PW 2 proved the measurement book, Exhibit 7, which clearly shows that the plaintiff had done extra work. Learned Subordinate Judge also found that the plaintiff had done some non-tender works, namely, MS grills for windows, collapsible gate, sanitary, electric works, earth development, painting, etc. Even after the defendants received the works done and goods delivered by the plaintiff, the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in refusing decree for such extra work. In support, he relied upon a decision in the case of Bengal Nagpur Railway Co Ltd vs Ruttanji Ramji and others. AIR 1935 Calcutta 347; Ram Pertab and others vs G Marshall. ILR 26 Calcutta 702 and Bazlur Rahman vs Bangladesh, 1990 BLD (AD) 66. 

 13. On the other hand, Mr Humayun Kabir Khadem, learned Advocate for the respondent, submits that as the work was done beyond the tender schedule and without the approval of the Hospital authority the plaintiff was not entitled to any decree for. such extra work. 

 14. Secondly, he submits the hospital was constructed for service to the poor and distressed people but ultimately, the hospital had to be transferred to the Bangladesh Bank. As the extra works, if any, were done without the approval of the governing body of the Hospital the plaintiff was not entitled to any decree for any amount for such extra works. 

 15. Defendants having not challenged the part decree, the issue facing us is as to whether or not the learned Subordinate Judge was justified in refusing a decree for the extra work done by the plaintiff during the construction of the Hospital. 

 28. The moot issue is now, whether or not the plaintiff is entitled to a decree for such extra works done and received by the defendants. 

 29. Only defence taken by the defendants is that as the works were done beyond the tender schedule and without the approval of the Hospital authority the plaintiff was not entitled to any decree for such work. Learned Subordinate Judge appears to have accepted such defence and refused a decree for such extra works. 

 39. In the circumstances; we find learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in refusing a decree for the works done by the plaintiff and received by the defendant. The appeal accordingly, succeeds. But the plaintiff will not get further compensation of Taka 2,19,380 as he claimed for retention of the final payment. 

 In the result, the appeal is allowed with cost. Impugned judgment and decree granting a money decree for Taka 2,43,500 are hereby affirmed and those refusing a decree for extra works are set aside. The suit is decreed for the extra work as well. The plaintiff will get a decree for 2,43,505 + 3,66,225.81 = Taka 6.09,730.81 with interest at the rate of 10% from the date of the decree till realisation.
